skillSays: Before writing any UI, look up each needed component (hero, form, card, select, toggle, badge...) in a 60+ component reference and follow its best practices.
Aim for modern, minimal, production-ready: restraint over decoration, an 8px spacing grid, one confident accent on a neutral palette.
Pair a distinctive display font with a clean body font and push weight contrast; avoid Inter/Roboto defaults, purple gradients and evenly spaced card grids.
Pick a design direction preset (Modern SaaS by default) and build real states: hover, focus, disabled, error, loading, empty.
Follow interaction rules: verb-first buttons, one primary per section, validate on blur, labels above inputs, 44px touch targets, WCAG AA contrast.
Avoid listed anti-patterns such as placeholder-only fields, equal-weight buttons, rainbow badges and disabled submit with no explanation.

changes: Hero follows the component page: split layout, one primary CTA plus one secondary, and a product panel on the right instead of decoration.
The panel's rows use consistent vertical lanes (time / avatar / name / status) with fixed-width slots and a limited semantic badge palette, as the List and Badge rules say.
Features break the 'evenly spaced card grid' rule: one tall dark card beside two stacked light ones, each media then title then meta then action, border only (no shadow).
Committed to Bricolage Grotesque 800 with tight tracking against Instrument Sans, and one cobalt accent on warm off-white.
The billing switch became a segmented control (the Segmented control rule: 2-5 options, animated sliding indicator) instead of a bare toggle, with a 'Save 20%' pill.
One shared bordered surface with three lanes rather than three floating shadow cards; only the Clinic lane gets a tint, badge and filled primary button.
Unavailable features are shown as muted lines so plans compare row by row, and prices animate in 220ms ease-out when the period changes.
Yearly shows the true yearly total and the amount saved under each price.
Form rules applied: single column, visible labels above inputs, placeholders only as format examples, native select with a prompt option, correct input types and autocomplete.
Validation runs on blur and re-checks as you type; on submit, focus moves to the first invalid field. Submit is never silently disabled.
Each error is inline under its field with an icon plus red border and tint, linked via aria-describedby; the terms control is a real checkbox, not a toggle.
Added a show-password control, a loading state on the button and a success state, covering the skill's 'graceful edge cases' bar.
